Train 1 leaves A at 09:10 toward B at 84 km/h. Distance A-B = 391 km. Train 2 leaves B at 10:05 toward A at 106 km/h. Bird starts at A together with first train and flies at 150 km/h back and forth between trains until they meet. Need when and where trains meet, and how far bird flies.

Need reason step by step and check every calculation.

Let's compute.

Let t be time after 09:10 in hours. Train1 position from A: x1 = 84 t, for t>=0. Train2 leaves at 10:05, which is 55 min after 09:10 = 55/60 = 11/12 h. For t >= 11/12, x2 = 391 - 106 (t - 11/12). Meet when x1 = x2.

84 t = 391 - 106(t - 11/12) = 391 - 106t + 106*11/12. 106*11/12 = (106/12)*11 = 53/6*11 = 583/6 = 97.1666667. So RHS = 391 + 583/6 - 106t = (2346/6 + 583/6) -106t = 2929/6 -106t. Equation: 84t +106t = 2929/6 => 190t = 2929/6 => t = 2929/(1140) hours. Simplify? 2929/1140. 1140*2=2280 remainder649. 649/1140=0.569298. t=2.569298 h = 2h + 0.569298*60=34.1579 min = 2h34m9.47s. Add to 09:10 => 11:44:09.47 approx. Need exact maybe 11:44:09.5.

Check alternative: At 10:05, train1 has traveled 84*(55/60)=84*11/12=7*11=77 km. Remaining distance = 391-77=314 km. Relative speed = 84+106=190 km/h. Time after 10:05 = 314/190 = 157/95 h = 1.6526316 h = 1h39m9.47s. Add 10:05 => 11:44:09.47. Same.

Where meet from A: x1 = 84*t = 84*2929/1140 = simplify 84/1140
